newsitem.title: USA: CBOT rice ends down on hedging, CBOT spillover.
newsitem.headline: CBOT rice ends down on hedging, CBOT spillover.

text.p: Spillover from other CBOT markets and hedging pressure on new crop contracts caused rice futures to end lower Monday, floor traders said.
"With the negative situation you've got on the floor--well, today it just closed in on rice," said one trader.
Traders also noted hedge pressure in September and November, and said that most of Monday's volume was spread trades.
In anticipation of first notice day on July 30, traders were rolling out of July positions into September or November, pit traders said.
Warm temperatures across the southern U.S. this past week were seen helping the newly planted rice crop and traders were looking for USDA's crop rating to show improvements.
Volume was estimated at 800 contracts, which would be below Friday's actual volume of 1,087 contracts.
Rice closed two to 10 cents per cwt lower, with July down ten at $11.57 per cwt.
